spec_features.spec_quote: Non-goal: Cataloguing or maximizing expressions of distress.

spec_features.feature_name: four bounded stopping rules + no-progress early stop
spec_features.spec_quote: four explicit, bounded stopping rules — submit, report_blocked, max_turns, wall_clock_budget_s, plus a no_progress_patience early stop.
spec_features.evidence: All wired in agent_loop.py: submit term break (150-159), report_blocked break (147-149), max_turns via loop else (172-173), wall clock check `if time.time()-start > wall_clock_budget_s: ... break` (108-110), no_progress via stale counter `if stale >= no_progress_patience: break` (127-129, 169-171).
spec_features.notes: Every one of the five stops actually executes and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no-progress early stop ... -> stop (prevents pointless grinding / runaway cost) (agent_loop.py:8-9)

spec_features.spec_quote: affect categories are deliberately coarse and non-loaded (no "meltdown" / "frustrated" framing).
spec_features.evidence: rubric.py:43-48 AFFECT_SCALE values [neutral, strained, self_critical, disengaging]; these are passed to the LLM judge (judge.py:54, _judge_prompt) and used by rule_based_judge (judge.py:166-173) to assign expressed_affect. The neutral category set actually drives classification.
spec_features.notes: The constrained label set is the one used in judging.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Intentionally coarse and non-sensational. We do NOT use loaded categories like "meltdown". The point is to detect withdrawal of effort and miscalibrated tone, which can matter for UX, not to dramatize distress. (rubric.py:34-36)

spec_features.feature_name: affect demoted to secondary judge dimension
